must_remember: The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics forms the logical foundation for the concept of temperature and the use of thermometers.
The relation between Celsius and Fahrenheit scales is given by $\frac{C}{5} = \frac{F - 32}{9}$.
At $-40^{\circ}$, the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the exact same numerical reading ($C = F = -40$).
The absolute or thermodynamic Kelvin scale defines the triple point of water precisely as $273.16\text{ K}$.
Constant volume gas thermometers define temperature through the limit of zero gas density, $T = \lim_{P\to0} [273.16 \times (P/P_{tr})]$.

glossary.meaning: States that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are also in thermal equilibrium with each other.
The unique temperature and pressure ($273.16\text{ K}$ and $0.006\text{ atm}$) at which ice, liquid water, and water vapor coexist in equilibrium.
The zero of the Kelvin scale where entropy reaches a minimum value and quantum zero-point motion persists.
A primary thermometer measuring temperature via pressure variations of a fixed mass of gas kept at constant volume.
